Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 8. People around you
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Live long
- Materials: Number cards, family photos, healthy-habits chart, COSYmanuals 'to be', 'numbers/dates', and 'present simple' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• state age and longevity milestones using numbers 1–100
• describe healthy living habits

Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

age — how old someone is. Example: What is your age?
year — a period of twelve months. Example: She is twenty years old.
healthy — well and strong. Example: He lives a healthy life.
life — the time you are alive. Example: She has a happy life.
exercise — physical activity. Example: Exercise is good for you.
food — things people eat. Example: The food is delicious.
happy — feeling good and positive. Example: I am happy today.
family — parents, children, and relatives. Example: My family is big.
old — not young; having lived a long time. Example: My grandfather is old.
live — to have your home in a place. Example: I live in Cairo.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• How old are you? (asking about age)
• I am ... years old. (stating age)
• She lives a healthy life. (describing lifestyle)
• He exercises every day. (describing a habit)
• They eat healthy food. (describing a habit)
• My grandfather is eighty. (stating an age)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'how old someone is'?
Which word means 'a period of twelve months'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Numbers 1–100 stress and the /j/ sound in 'year'

year /jɪə/ — starts with /j/
healthy /ˈhelθi/ — voiced th
exercise /ˈeksəsaɪz/ — stress the first syllable
eighty /ˈeɪti/ — long /eɪ/

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'be' to say who someone is, how they feel, and where they are from.

Form:
The verb 'to be': I am / You are / He, she, it is / We are / They are. Negative: I'm not, isn't, aren't. Question: Am I...? Are you...? Is he...?

Examples:
• I am a student.
• She is from Spain.
• We are happy today.
• They are not teachers.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
My name ___ Alex.
They ___ from Italy.
I ___ tired today.
She ___ not a teacher.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I am ... (a student / happy / from Egypt).
• She is ... (a teacher / tired / from Spain).
• They are ... (students / at home / happy).
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• Are you a student? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
• Is she from France? — Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.
• Are they happy? — Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write two true sentences with 'I am...' and 'I am not...'.
• Introduce two people in the class with 'He/She is...'.
Reading: Live long

My grandfather is eighty years old. He lives a healthy life. He exercises every day and eats healthy food. He is happy and active. My grandmother is seventy-five. She loves gardening and cooking. They live with our family. We are happy together. How old are the people in your family?
How old is the grandfather?
What does the grandmother love?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: How old is your grandfather?
B: He is eighty years old.
A: Does he exercise?
B: Yes, he does. He exercises every day.
A: What does he eat?
B: He eats healthy food and drinks water.
How old is the grandfather?
How often does he exercise?
Speaking task: Ask your partner about the ages of three family members and their healthy habits.

• How old are you?
• Who is the oldest person in your family?
• What do you do to stay healthy?
• Do you exercise every day?
• What food is healthy?
Role-play: You are interviewing a 90-year-old person about their life and healthy habits.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about age and healthy habits in your family.
Model: My ... is ... years old. He/She ... every day.
